content.title: About
content.content: Raw peaches are juicy fruits of the peach tree (Prunus persica), native to Central Asia and cultivated for over 4,000 years. They have a sweet aroma, tender flesh, and a slightly tart flavor. Peaches are typically eaten fresh but are also used in cooking, baking, and juice production.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peaches belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to plums, apricots, and cherries.
Peach skin is rich in antioxidants, including vitamin C and carotenoids.
The seed (pit) contains amygdalin, which can release cyanide when broken down, so it should not be eaten raw.
Peaches were prized in ancient China for their medicinal properties, especially for aiding digestion.
There are more than 2,000 peach varieties, differing in flavor, color, and size.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps regulate blood sugar levels, and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance, normal heart function, and muscle activity.

items.title: Contains beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, which is important for vision and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie fruit
items.content: Peaches are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peaches, ranging from skin rashes to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Peaches contain natural sugars; people with diabetes should account for them in their diet.

items.title: Pit hazard
items.content: The hard pit can be a choking hazard for young children and should be removed before serving.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Like many fruits, peaches may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw peaches can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, oatmeal, smoothies, and desserts. They can be sliced, baked, or used to make compotes. The skin is edible and nutrient‑dense, though it can be peeled if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peaches at room temperature until they ripen, then transfer to the refrigerator where they stay fresh for up to 5 days. Avoid airtight containers, which can accelerate ripening and cause mold.
